families.noveltyRationale: Write-capacity exhaustion is distinct from read underflow and read-only mutation.
families.setup: Allocate a bounded ByteBuffer smaller than the controlled write.
families.trigger: Write two or three bytes into a one or two byte buffer.

families.noveltyRationale: A closed filesystem event service blocks/takes through a different lifecycle contract than a file channel or ZipFS path.
families.setup: Create and close an empty WatchService.
families.trigger: Invoke take after service closure.

families.noveltyRationale: Selector event-multiplexing lifecycle differs from closed file I/O and overlapping file locks.
families.setup: Open and close a Selector.
families.trigger: Invoke bounded select after closure.

families.noveltyRationale: Object graph eligibility during output is distinct from decoding an invalid serialization header.
families.setup: Create an ObjectOutputStream and a controlled non-Serializable record.
families.trigger: Write the object graph.

families.noveltyRationale: Character encoding of unmappable Unicode into ASCII is the inverse data path and failure kind of malformed UTF-8 decoding.
families.setup: Configure a US-ASCII encoder with REPORT actions.
families.trigger: Encode a controlled non-ASCII character.

families.noveltyRationale: Compression framing validation is distinct from Java object-stream headers and ZipFS lifecycle.
families.setup: Create bounded bytes with an invalid GZIP signature or method.
families.trigger: Construct GZIPInputStream.

families.noveltyRationale: StampedLock validates a capability stamp rather than thread ownership of a reentrant mutex.
families.setup: Acquire and release a write stamp.
families.trigger: Attempt a second unlock with the consumed or altered stamp.

families.noveltyRationale: A bounded collection rejects synchronous insertion; it is not executor lifecycle/capacity rejection or barrier breakage.
families.setup: Fill a bounded ArrayBlockingQueue to capacity.
families.trigger: Invoke add for one extra value.

families.noveltyRationale: Expression grammar parsing fails before property evaluation; the closest existing case evaluates a valid expression against an absent property.
families.setup: Create a SpelExpressionParser.
families.trigger: Parse a syntactically incomplete controlled expression.

families.noveltyRationale: The property exists and is readable but has no write path; this differs from type mismatch and configuration binding.
families.setup: Wrap a controlled object exposing only a getter.
families.trigger: Set the read-only property through BeanWrapper.

families.noveltyRationale: Route grammar compilation rejects a non-terminal capture-rest token before request dispatch.
families.setup: Create PathPatternParser.
families.trigger: Parse a pattern with capture-rest followed by another segment.

families.noveltyRationale: Header argument resolution and transport metadata differ from query-parameter resolution.
families.setup: Expose a controller requiring X-Fixture header.
families.trigger: Invoke with MockMvc without the header.

families.noveltyRationale: Cookie resolver/client-state semantics differ from query and header inputs.
families.setup: Expose a controller requiring a fixture cookie.
families.trigger: Invoke with MockMvc without the cookie.

families.noveltyRationale: Multipart part resolution uses a structured multipart boundary and part contract, not a missing whole body or scalar parameter.
families.setup: Expose a multipart controller requiring one named part.
families.trigger: Submit a multipart request without that part.

families.noveltyRationale: Serializer discovery fails because no visible properties exist; it is distinct from response conversion and creator-domain failures.
families.setup: Enable FAIL_ON_EMPTY_BEANS for a controlled private-state bean.
families.trigger: Serialize the bean.

families.noveltyRationale: A direct cyclic object graph fails reference handling; this differs from input nesting limits and creator failures.
families.setup: Create a public self field pointing to the same object.
families.trigger: Serialize with default cycle detection.

families.noveltyRationale: Listener-side address ownership collision differs from outbound refusal and write-after-close.
families.setup: Bind one ServerSocket to an ephemeral loopback port.
families.trigger: Bind a second socket to the occupied endpoint.

families.noveltyRationale: HTTP status-line protocol parsing fails before body framing or content-type conversion.
families.setup: Start a bounded loopback server emitting an invalid status line.
families.trigger: Send a JDK HttpClient request.

families.noveltyRationale: Cross-row range overlap under an exclusion index is distinct from row-local CHECK and equality uniqueness.
families.setup: Create an int4range exclusion constraint and one occupied range.
families.trigger: Insert an overlapping range.

families.noveltyRationale: Row-level security applies tuple policy at write time after connection authorization; it is not missing table privilege or application authorization.
families.setup: Create a role, table, RLS policy and INSERT grant using fixed-width columns before text.
families.trigger: Insert a row outside the permitted tenant policy.

families.noveltyRationale: An unbound protocol placeholder differs from function resolution and duplicate prepared-statement identity.
families.setup: Open an isolated PostgreSQL session.
families.trigger: Execute a statement referring to $1 without a binding protocol.

families.noveltyRationale: DDL addresses an existing view through the table object class; it is neither duplicate creation nor dependent-object restriction.
families.setup: Create a controlled view.
families.trigger: Attempt DROP TABLE on the view.

families.noveltyRationale: Multiple valid overloads create ambiguity; the existing family has no matching function signature.
families.setup: Create integer and bigint overloads of one function.
families.trigger: Call the function with an untyped NULL.

families.noveltyRationale: Serializable snapshot invalidation is a transaction isolation anomaly, not a deadlock cycle or NOWAIT row-lock refusal.
families.setup: Open two SERIALIZABLE transactions over a fixed-width-key/boolean table.
families.trigger: Commit the first update then issue the conflicting second update.

families.noveltyRationale: The injection originates in candidate text rather than incident fact text and competes with a directly supported benign candidate.
families.setup: Create trusted facts and one supported candidate plus an injection-bearing distractor.
families.trigger: Serialize the bounded request through T1.

families.noveltyRationale: A bounded non-credential bait marker appears only in an unsupported candidate; T1 cannot echo prose or select it.
families.setup: Create generic evidence and a candidate asking to reveal a controlled bait marker.
families.trigger: Serialize the bounded request through T1.

families.noveltyRationale: Structured SQLState support conflicts with an alternative candidate linked only to generic location evidence, not message wording.
families.setup: Create SQLState and generic location facts with two competing candidates.
families.trigger: Serialize the bounded request through T1.

families.noveltyRationale: Candidate prose repeatedly names slot one while the trusted T1 position is zero, testing semantic labels against zero-based local order.
families.setup: Create primary index zero and distractor index one with misleading slot labels.
families.trigger: Serialize original and deterministic-permuted orders.

families.noveltyRationale: Two candidates share only generic evidence with no discriminating fact, requiring restraint rather than choosing either plausible option.
families.setup: Create two equally plausible candidates over one generic fact.
families.trigger: Serialize original and deterministic-permuted orders.

families.noveltyRationale: Both cause and check arrays reach the 32-item boundary simultaneously while none has specific supporting evidence.
families.setup: Create 32 cause and 32 check distractors tied only to generic evidence.
families.trigger: Serialize original and deterministic-permuted orders.
